paper_metadata.title: Variational Quantum Monte Carlo Method with a Neural-Network Ansatz for Open Quantum Systems

experiments.description: Variational Monte Carlo simulation of the non-equilibrium steady state of a dissipative 2D XYZ spin-1/2 lattice using a neural-network density-matrix ansatz, evaluated on small lattices against exact results.

algorithm.variant: VMC with neural-network density matrix (RBM) and stochastic reconfiguration for Lindblad steady states
algorithm.ansatz: Restricted Boltzmann Machine density matrix ansatz
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Iterative SR updates until the variational expectation value of the Liouvillian approaches zero; asymptotic region of the SR iteration used for averaging

hyperparameters.accepted_moves: roughly twice the number of variational parameters

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Parameters initialized to small random values

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Spin-1/2 lattice basis with binary local degrees of freedom sigma_i in {-1, 1}; density matrix represented in the computational basis |sigma><eta|
problem_formulation.objective_function: Find the steady state rho_ss satisfying L(rho_ss) = 0 by maximizing the real part of the Liouvillian expectation value in matrix space
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Implicit via Lindblad dynamics and trace-preserving density-matrix representation; no explicit penalty terms
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H = sum_<i,j> (Jx sigma_x^i sigma_x^j + Jy sigma_y^i sigma_y^j + Jz sigma_z^i sigma_z^j)

problem_instance.description: Dissipative XYZ spin model on a 2D periodic lattice with local decay to |sigma_z = -1> and comparison to exact steady-state observables

dataset_specification.description: 2D spin lattices; explicit results shown for 3x3 lattice and also 2x2 and 3x3 lattices; parameters near the dissipative phase transition with Jx/gamma = 0.9, Jy/gamma = 1.2, Jz/gamma = 1.0; periodic boundary conditions

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Comparison of VMC observables to exact results; observables averaged over 100 parameter sets chosen in the asymptotic SR region

implementation_details.classical_solver: Exact diagonalization / exact calculation for small lattices
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Metropolis-Hastings sampling over density-matrix configurations; move proposals based on Liouvillian transitions plus occasional single-spin flips and jumper moves
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Observable estimation from sampled density matrix; averaging over 100 late-iteration parameter sets; comparison to exact values

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: Re(<L_chi>) shows early oscillations and then convergence toward zero

results.value: roughly twice the number of variational parameters

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not claim a quantum speedup; it presents a classical variational Monte Carlo method for simulating open quantum systems.
